terms-related-to-anatomy-physiology.definition: Study of changes in the function of a body system caused by disease
Study of the nature and cause of abnormal conditions.
Study of the cause of disease.
Anatomy is the study of the parts or structurers of the body.
Physiology is the study of how the body parts work.
A grouping of a number of cells together to form something that is larger and more complex than a single cell (e.g. muscle, bone).
The cell is the basic structural unit of the body. Each cell is specialized. Specialized cells are grouped together to form tissue. The material that makes up the cell is called protoplasm.
It includes the Cell Membrane, Cytoplasm, and Nucleus
The structure that surrounds and protects the cell.
The material located inside the cell that is not part of the nucleus.
The powerhouse of the cell that sustains the life of the cell. Because of the chromosomes, it allows the cell to reproduce.
Tissue is a group or layer of similarly specialized cells that join together to perform certain specific functions.
The root hist means tissue and the suffix -logy means study of therefore its is the study of tissue.
Covers both the internal and external surfaces of the body.
Holds the organs of the body in place and binds all parts of the body together. Types of connective tissues are: bone, cartilage, and adipose or 'fat'.
Lack of development of tissue or an organ. (Prefix 'a' means without).
Incomplete development of tissue or an organ. (Prefix 'hypo' means below, decreased or deficient)
Abnormal increase in the number of normal cells in a tissue. (Prefix 'hyper' means above, increased or excessive).
Abnormal development or growth of cells. (Prefix 'dys' means difficult, painful or bad).
Change in the structure of cells and their orientation to each other. (Prefix 'an' means without)
A gland is a group of specialized cellls that secrete a material used somewhere else in the body. The root for gland is 'aden/o'.
A type of gland that secretes their substances into ducts that take it to the area of the body where it will be used, e.g. the sweat gland.

A type of glad that don't have ducts and their secretions flow directly into the blood stream. The blood transports the secretions to the area of the body where it will be used, e.g. the thyroid gland.
A gland in the body which functions both as an exocrine and endocrine.

body-systems.definition: Support and shape the body. Protection, storage of minerals, and production of blood cells.
Movement of the body. Holds the body erect and generates body heat.
Carries food and needed oxygen to body cells.
Provides nutrients and removes waste from the tissue. Protects the body from harmful substances.
Brings oxygen into the body for use by the cells and removes the waste product carbon dioxide.
Digestion of food and absorption of the nutrients needed for life. Elimination of solid body wastes.
Filters blood to remove waste products and maintain the right fluid balance in the body.
Coordinating mechanism within the body. Transmits messages throughout the body.
Protection of the body. Controls temperature and water regulation.
